reasons: The principle of one dwelling on this site is considered acceptable. The site is part of a domestic garden within the Doncaster Main Urban Area, in a Residential Policy Area, outside the Green Belt and within Flood Zone 1. A single windfall dwelling on a small plot in a sustainable urban location makes effective use of land, and previous permissions for a dwelling on this plot support the principle. This is in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 1 and 10 and NPPF paragraphs 124 and 125. Detailed matters of amenity, character and design are tested under the other reasons and at reserved matters stage.

The effect on the character and appearance of the Bessacarr Conservation Area is considered capable of being acceptable. The indicative form, with front dormers, buff brick and clay tiles, is plausible for the street. The scheme does not show ridge height or site levels, and frontage trees would be removed. The outline application reserves all matters, so no harm is demonstrated at this stage. Conditions requiring details of scale, levels, materials, landscaping and a heritage assessment at reserved matters stage can secure a scheme that preserves the character and appearance of the conservation area, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 37 and NPPF paragraphs 207, 208, 212 and 215.

The design, scale and character of the proposal are considered capable of being acceptable. A single dormer bungalow on a 575 sq m plot with a 22.0m frontage is not objectionable in principle. Its height, massing and relationship to ground levels cannot yet be fully judged, so these can be controlled at reserved matters stage. Conditions limiting the building to one and a half storeys and requiring sections, levels and materials will secure a dwelling that responds to its context, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 41, 42 and 44 and NPPF paragraphs 135 and 139.

The effect on neighbouring residential amenity is considered capable of being acceptable. The indicative layout shows 26.0m separation to No. 74 and 8.0m from the flank to 6 Middlefield Road. The side elevations have minimal openings and the plot is generous. Levels and ridge height are not yet shown, but these can be tested at reserved matters stage. Conditions on levels, side-elevation glazing and construction management will protect neighbouring living conditions, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 10, 44 and 45 and NPPF paragraph 135.

The access and parking arrangements are considered acceptable. A single dwelling would generate very little traffic. The amended site plan shows a 4.5m dropped crossing onto Middlefield Road and two off-street parking spaces, with an integral garage on the indicative plans. No unacceptable highway safety impact or severe cumulative impact is demonstrated. Details of access, visibility, parking, cycle and bin storage, electric vehicle charging and construction management can be secured by condition, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 13 and NPPF paragraphs 115, 116 and 117.

The effect on trees and ecology is considered capable of being made acceptable. Trees T9 and T10 at the frontage and other garden trees are shown for removal, and no arboricultural or ecological information has been submitted. These gaps can be addressed through conditions requiring a tree survey and protection plan, an ecological appraisal with enhancement measures, controls on nesting season clearance, replacement planting, and confirmation of the biodiversity gain position, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 29, 30, 32 and 48 and NPPF paragraphs 136, 187 and 193.

The proposal is considered acceptable in terms of flood risk and drainage. The site is in Flood Zone 1 and a single dwelling is minor development, so no sequential or exception test is required. Yorkshire Water raises no objection. The surface water discharge hierarchy and discharge rate can be secured by condition, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 56 and 57, NPPF paragraphs 181 and 182 and paragraph 5.2.4 of the Flood Risk SPD.

The proposal is considered acceptable in terms of contamination and pollution. The site is part of an existing domestic garden, and the application states that the land is not known or suspected to be contaminated. The reported historic ground movement at the rear boundary level change is unevidenced. It can be addressed through a precautionary risk assessment, a topographical survey and a ground stability assessment at reserved matters stage, together with construction environmental controls, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 54 and 55 and NPPF paragraphs 187, 196 and 198.
conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: Required by Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans and documents listed on the decision notice. Reason: To ensure that the development is carried out in accordance with the application as approved.

Approval of the details of the layout, scale, appearance, access and landscaping of the development (the reserved matters) shall be obtained from the Local Planning Authority before any development commences. The reserved matters applications shall be accompanied by a topographical survey, accurate site sections and street-scene elevations showing existing and proposed ground levels, finished floor levels, and ridge and eaves heights in relation to 6 Middlefield Road, 74 Market Lane and the Middlefield Road frontage. They shall also include a heritage impact assessment demonstrating that the scale, form and materials respect the Bessacarr Conservation Area, and an assessment of ground stability with details of any retaining or boundary treatment needed at the rear boundary level change. The development shall be carried out at the approved levels and heights. Reason: To ensure the scale and massing of the dwelling respond to the character and appearance of the Bessacarr Conservation Area, to protect neighbouring living conditions, and to ensure ground conditions are properly treated, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 37, 41, 44 and 55.

The dwelling shall be no more than one and a half storeys, with accommodation in the roof space served by dormer windows, and its ridge height shall not exceed the maximum height approved at reserved matters stage. Reason: To keep the building to a scale sympathetic to its context and subsidiary in the street scene, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 37 and 44.

No development above foundation level shall take place until samples or full details of the external wall, roof, window and hard-surfacing materials have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, and the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To ensure a high quality appearance that preserves the character and appearance of the Bessacarr Conservation Area, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 37 and 41 and NPPF paragraph 135.

The reserved matters submission shall include a hard and soft landscaping scheme showing the retention and protection of frontage and boundary hedging and retained trees, native replacement tree and hedgerow planting, boundary treatments, and a maintenance and management regime for at least five years. The approved scheme shall be implemented in the first planting season following occupation. Reason: To soften the development, compensate for tree loss, retain the verdant character of Middlefield Road and maintain the character of the conservation area, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 32, 37, 41, 44 and 48.

The reserved matters submission shall demonstrate that no first-floor or roof-level windows in the side elevations will overlook neighbouring properties. Any such windows shall be obscure glazed and non-opening below 1.7m above floor level unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To protect neighbouring privacy in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 44.

No development shall take place until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. It shall cover working hours, contractor parking, delivery and construction vehicle routing and times, wheel cleaning, dust suppression, control of construction noise, and measures to keep Middlefield Road clear of obstruction. The approved plan shall be implemented throughout construction. Reason: In the interests of highway safety and the amenity of nearby residents, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 10, 13 and 54.

The reserved matters submission shall include details of the vehicular access, dropped crossing, visibility splays, and on-site parking and turning, with parking provision in line with Appendix 6 of the Doncaster Local Plan. The dwelling shall not be occupied until the access and parking areas have been constructed in accordance with the approved details, surfaced in a bound material and drained so as not to discharge onto the highway, and they shall be retained for that use thereafter. Reason: To ensure safe and suitable access and adequate off-street parking, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 13 and NPPF paragraph 115.

Prior to occupation of the dwelling, secure cycle storage, a bin storage and collection point within the curtilage with level access to the highway boundary, and an electric vehicle charging point shall be provided in accordance with details submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These shall be retained thereafter. Reason: To promote sustainable travel and prevent waste containers being stored on the highway, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 13.

No development shall take place until a BS5837 tree survey, arboricultural impact assessment and tree protection plan have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved protection measures shall be installed before any equipment, machinery or materials are brought onto the site and retained throughout construction. Reason: To ensure trees and hedgerows of public amenity and ecological value are adequately protected, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 32 and 37.

No development shall take place until a preliminary ecological appraisal, including any necessary protected species surveys, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, together with details of mitigation and biodiversity enhancement features such as bat and bird boxes and hedgehog gaps. The approved measures shall be implemented in full. No tree or hedgerow clearance shall take place between 1 March and 31 August inclusive unless a suitably qualified ecologist has first confirmed in writing that no active nests are present. Reason: To protect species and secure biodiversity enhancement, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 29 and 30 and NPPF paragraphs 187 and 193.

Development shall not begin until either a biodiversity gain plan has been approved by the Local Planning Authority, or written evidence has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority confirming that the development is exempt from the biodiversity gain condition. Reason: To meet the statutory biodiversity gain requirement, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 30.

The site shall be developed with separate systems of drainage for foul and surface water on and off site. No piped discharge of surface water shall take place until surface water drainage works have been completed in accordance with details submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with the sewerage undertaker. If discharge to the public sewer is proposed, the details shall include evidence that infiltration and discharge to a watercourse have been properly considered and why they have been discounted, and shall limit the discharge rate to no more than 3.5 litres per second. Reason: To ensure satisfactory and sustainable drainage and that no surface water discharges take place until proper provision has been made for its disposal, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 56.

Prior to the commencement of development, a Preliminary Risk Assessment (desk study) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. If it identifies potential contamination or ground instability risks, a site investigation and, where necessary, a remediation strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing, and the approved remediation shall be completed and verified before the dwelling is first occupied. If contamination not previously identified is found during development, work shall cease and the Local Planning Authority shall be notified, and no further development shall take place until a remediation strategy has been approved in writing and implemented. Reason: To ensure the land is suitable for residential use and to safeguard human health and the environment, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 55 and NPPF paragraph 196.
